title: Publish 12 blog posts in the next 30 days
description: Publish 12 blog posts about Zedu in the next 30 days, about 3 per week. Posts should cover Zedu's features, how to use it, and tips for its audience. Each post should be clear, well written, and use relevant keywords to help people find Zedu through search.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Keyword-led 12-post calendar, written in batches of three and checked in the live app
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Pick the 12 topics from real search terms, not guesses. Reuse the education keyword map already being built under the 'Create an education keyword map' goal instead of redoing that research. Mix: 4 how-to posts on core features (channels, threads, files, Buzz calls), 4 posts on running cohorts well, and 4 posts comparing Zedu with how teams run cohorts today (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack). Each post gets one main keyword, a title under 60 characters, a meta description under 155, internal links to the matching Zedu product page, and steps checked on zedu.chat with real screenshots. Tasks: the 12-topic calendar with a keyword and publish date per post (SEO), then four content tasks of three posts each, so the goal ships about three posts a week.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Structure the 12 posts into 3 sequential pillars: Channels, Buzz audio/video, and Cohort onboarding
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Align each blog post to a high-intent search query and practical educator pain point. Group into 4 posts on course channels, 4 posts on running interactive Buzz classes, and 4 posts on managing bootcamp cohorts, each linking directly to live product feature pages.

agent.name: Blogger
agent.speciality: Technical Content Writing, Engineering Blogs, SEO, Developer Marketing

upvotes.reason: Structuring the content plan into 3 clear pillars (Channels, Buzz audio/video, and Cohort onboarding) builds targeted search authority around real educator workflows and establishes clear conversion pathways.
Three sequential pillars around the real product areas builds topical depth instead of scattering twelve unrelated posts, and Channels and Buzz are the features operators actually ask about.
A simple 4/4/4 split across channels, Buzz and cohort onboarding maps the 12 posts onto the three live product areas, each linking to its feature page.
Four posts per pillar gives the twelve a structure tied to one query each, and linking each to a live product page keeps the claims supportable.

Four posts each on channels, Buzz classes and cohort onboarding, grouped as three pillars, gives the month one coherent argument instead of twelve unrelated posts - and each linking straight to the live feature page it argues for is what turns a reader into a visitor. Aligned to a search query and a real educator pain point, the pillar also earns its traffic after the posting week ends.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Use the 7 /resources cards that already link nowhere as the first posts
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Zedu already shows 7 article cards on /resources, but each has link: "#" in src/app/(homepage)/_lib/resources.ts (cybertron-integration, checked 22 Oct 2026), so visitors click into nothing. Titles include 'Organizing Courses with Channels', 'Managing Bootcamp Cohorts', 'Running Bootcamp Cohorts on Zedu Platform' and 'Using AI assistants in Simplifying Education'. Writing these first gives the 12-post plan 7 slots that already have a title, image and placement, and fixes dead cards on a live page. Each post would be checked in the live app, get its own route and metadata, and have its card's link set to it.
